title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-18
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: A pristine soundboard capture of the Tampa show delivers a crisp mix and a legendary second‑set climax (Weather Report Suite → Dark Star → Drums → Eyes of the World → Wharf Rat).
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller‑sourced soundboard is praised for its clear stereo field, minimal patch issues and overall fidelity, making the performance shine.  Musically the concert is highlighted by a rare Tennessee Jed opener, a superb China Cat → Rider jam, and an unforgettable Weather Report Suite/Dark Star/Drums/Eyes of the World/Wharf Rat sequence that many reviewers call one of ’73’s best.  The first set is noted as slower‑moving but still solid, while the second set erupts with jazz‑laden energy.

ai_rating.rationale: Over two dozen reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 stars, repeatedly praising both performance and mix; only a few minor criticisms of first‑set pacing exist, yielding a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced stereo soundboard with good stage separation; occasional audience patch noted but not detrimental to listening experience.

standout_songs: Weather Report Suite → Dark Star → Drums → Eyes of the World → Wharf Rat
poor_songs: First set overall (described as moving a bit slowly)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Rare Tennessee Jed opener sets an unusual tone; first set mixes slower ballads with upbeat numbers, while the second set builds relentless momentum and showcases the band’s late‑’73 jazz‑rock peak.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring solos (especially in Weather Report Suite, Dark Star, Eyes of the World) and confident vocal delivery; noted as “on fire” throughout the second set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for aggressive, low‑register bass work, monster leads on Eyes of the World, and strong interplay with the rest of the band.
band_member_comments.Bob: Recognized for jazzy, slashing leads in the first set and energetic rhythm guitar; notable interplay with Lesh during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is described as “ready to play,” delivering solid piano fills on Me and My Uncle, El Paso, and throughout the show; overall keyboard work praised despite Donna Jean’s absence.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann noted for staying “in the pocket” with a tight groove, especially during the drum solo that leads into Eyes of the World.
